---
title: "Network from Lines"
date: 2026-09-12
categories: [tool, network]
description: "Turn a roads or rivers layer into a graph — nodes, edges, connected components — and see exactly how much a snap tolerance changes the answer. Free, runs entirely in your browser: the file never leaves your computer."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a line layer (roads, rivers, any network of `LineString`
features) and build a graph from it: nodes at the line endpoints, edges
along the lines themselves. A line network is only ever as connected as
its own noding — two segments that were meant to meet but miss by a few
centimeters become two separate pieces of the graph unless you tell the
tool how close counts as "the same point". The snap tolerance slider
below makes that decision visible instead of silent.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

```{.webgeods-python #network-example-py}
#| package: geopandas
import json

# A deliberately instructive example, not just "some lines": a closed
# block (4 edges, one connected piece), a fully separate cluster
# elsewhere on the map, and a "spur" whose first endpoint sits about
# 4m from the block's corner -- not exactly on it. At snap tolerance 0
# that gap makes 3 components; raise the tolerance past ~4m and the
# spur joins the block, leaving 2. That gap IS the lesson this tool
# teaches -- a network is only as connected as its noding.
features = [
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "block-n"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.4500, 41.9000], [12.4520, 41.9000]]}},
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "block-e"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.4520, 41.9000], [12.4520, 41.9020]]}},
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "block-s"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.4520, 41.9020], [12.4500, 41.9020]]}},
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "block-w"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.4500, 41.9020], [12.4500, 41.9000]]}},
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "spur-1"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.45205, 41.9000], [12.4540, 41.9000]]}},
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "spur-2"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.4540, 41.9000], [12.4540, 41.9020]]}},
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "island-1"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.4700, 41.9100], [12.4720, 41.9100]]}},
    {"type": "Feature", "properties": {"name": "island-2"},
     "geometry": {"type": "LineString", "coordinates": [[12.4720, 41.9100], [12.4720, 41.9120]]}},
]

with open("/uploaded.geojson", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": features}, f)

{"written": "/uploaded.geojson", "lines": len(features)}
```

```{.webgeods-python #network-inspect-py}
#| package: geopandas
import geopandas as gpd

EMPTY_FC = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}

gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

crs_warning = None
summary_out = None
if gdf is not None:
    if gdf.crs is None:
        gdf = gdf.set_crs("EPSG:4326")
        crs_warning = "No CRS found in the uploaded file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."
    elif str(gdf.crs) != "EPSG:4326":
        gdf = gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    line_mask = gdf.geometry.geom_type.isin(["LineString", "MultiLineString"])
    dropped = int((~line_mask).sum())
    gdf = gdf[line_mask].reset_index(drop=True)

    summary_out = {
        "count": int(len(gdf)),
        "dropped": dropped,
        "crs": str(gdf.crs)
    }

{
    "features": gdf.__geo_interface__ if gdf is not None else EMPTY_FC,
    "crsWarning": crs_warning,
    "summary": summary_out
}
```

```{.webgeods-python #network-build-py}
#| package: geopandas, igraph
#| inject: snapTolerance
import numpy as np
import geopandas as gpd
import igraph as ig
from shapely.geometry import Point

if "gdf" not in globals() or gdf is None or len(gdf) == 0:
    raise RuntimeError("Run Inspect first (upload a file or load the example) before building a graph.")

gdf_lines = gdf.explode(index_parts=False).reset_index(drop=True)

# Metric working CRS: a snap tolerance and an edge length are real
# distances, so they can't be computed in degrees. Same bbox-center
# UTM auto-pick already used by Buffer & Proximity and Spatial
# Clustering elsewhere on this site.
minx, miny, maxx, maxy = gdf_lines.total_bounds
center_lon = float((minx + maxx) / 2)
center_lat = float((miny + maxy) / 2)
utm_zone = int((center_lon + 180) // 6) + 1
calc_epsg = (32600 if center_lat >= 0 else 32700) + utm_zone
gdf_proj = gdf_lines.to_crs(epsg=calc_epsg)

# Endpoints only: interior vertices are the line's SHAPE, not its
# topology. One line feature = one edge between its two ends; the edge
# keeps its real geometry on the map, not a straight chord.
ends = np.array([
    c for geom in gdf_proj.geometry
    for c in (geom.coords[0][:2], geom.coords[-1][:2])
], dtype=float)

tolerance = max(0.0, float(snapTolerance))

# Pairwise distance check (not grid rounding: rounding silently fails
# to merge two endpoints a few cm apart that happen to straddle a cell
# boundary -- exactly the failure mode a snap tolerance exists to
# prevent) via plain numpy broadcasting rather than a KD-tree -- scipy
# isn't vendored on this site and adding it just for this would repeat
# the same "hidden weight" mistake already found and avoided with
# networkx (which would have pulled in matplotlib). O(n^2) in the
# number of endpoints, which is fine at this tool's scale; a large
# upload would want a spatial index instead. A tiny floor (well under
# a millimeter) instead of a literal 0 absorbs floating-point noise
# from independent coordinate literals/serialization without changing
# what "0 tolerance" means in practice.
tol = max(tolerance, 1e-9)
diff = ends[:, None, :] - ends[None, :, :]
dist = np.sqrt((diff ** 2).sum(axis=2))
upper = np.triu(np.ones(dist.shape, dtype=bool), k=1)
pairs = np.argwhere((dist <= tol) & upper)

parent = list(range(len(ends)))

def find(i):
    while parent[i] != i:
        parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]
        i = parent[i]
    return i

for a, b in pairs:
    ra, rb = find(int(a)), find(int(b))
    if ra != rb:
        parent[rb] = ra

node_of = [find(i) for i in range(len(ends))]
unique_nodes = sorted(set(node_of))
node_index = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(unique_nodes)}

# MultiGraph-equivalent: igraph allows parallel edges by default (no
# simplify() call below), since two distinct roads between the same
# pair of junctions are two real edges -- collapsing them would
# under-report both the edge count and the total length.
edges = [
    (node_index[node_of[2 * i]], node_index[node_of[2 * i + 1]])
    for i in range(len(gdf_proj))
]
lengths = [float(geom.length) for geom in gdf_proj.geometry]

g = ig.Graph(n=len(unique_nodes), edges=edges, directed=False)

components = g.connected_components()
membership = list(components.membership)
sizes = components.sizes()
order = sorted(range(len(sizes)), key=lambda c: sizes[c], reverse=True)
rank_of = {c: r for r, c in enumerate(order)}
component_of_vertex = [rank_of[c] for c in membership]

degrees = g.degree()

# Node representative = the MEAN of its snapped members, not an
# arbitrary one -- a junction snapped from several endpoints sits in
# their middle instead of jumping to whichever line happened to be
# read first.
reps = {}
for i, n in enumerate(node_of):
    reps.setdefault(node_index[n], []).append(ends[i])

node_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "node": list(range(len(unique_nodes))),
        "degree": degrees,
        "component": component_of_vertex
    },
    geometry=[Point(np.mean(reps[i], axis=0)) for i in range(len(unique_nodes))],
    crs=gdf_proj.crs
).to_crs("EPSG:4326")

edge_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "edge": list(range(len(edges))),
        # "source"/"target" reference node_gdf's own "node" ids -- read
        # by the force-directed diagram panel (shared/graph-diagram.js)
        # to build its link list; unused by the map layer itself.
        "source": [u for u, v in edges],
        "target": [v for u, v in edges],
        "lengthM": [round(l, 2) for l in lengths],
        "component": [component_of_vertex[u] for u, v in edges]
    },
    geometry=list(gdf_lines.geometry),
    crs="EPSG:4326"
)

total_m = sum(lengths)

{
    "nodes": node_gdf.__geo_interface__,
    "edges": edge_gdf.__geo_interface__,
    # matchPaint() keys on these; capped at 5 so the legend stays
    # readable -- everything past that falls through to matchPaint's
    # own fallback color, which is exactly what that fallback is for.
    "componentIds": list(range(min(5, len(sizes)))),
    "summary": {
        "lines": int(len(gdf_lines)),
        "nodes": int(g.vcount()),
        "edges": int(g.ecount()),
        "components": len(sizes),
        "largestComponentNodes": int(sizes[order[0]]) if sizes else 0,
        "deadEnds": int(sum(1 for d in degrees if d == 1)),
        "intersections": int(sum(1 for d in degrees if d >= 3)),
        "meanDegree": round(2 * g.ecount() / max(1, g.vcount()), 2),
        "maxDegree": int(max(degrees)) if degrees else 0,
        "totalLengthKm": round(total_m / 1000, 3),
        "snapTolerance": tolerance,
        "calculationCrs": f"EPSG:{calc_epsg}"
    }
}
```

*First run loads the Python engine — expect 30-40 seconds. Instant
after that, and again each time you come back to this page.*

<div id="nfl-dashboard"></div>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {

  // Bidirectional cross-link: the ONE function both the diagram's own
  // click handler and the map's click handler call, so "select node
  // N" always means the same thing regardless of which view triggered
  // it -- highlights on the map AND marks it selected in the diagram,
  // every time, from either direction. Looked up fresh each call
  // (rather than closing over the `dashboard` variable declared
  // below) so it reads the CURRENT map/diagram instances either way.
  function selectNode(id) {

    const dash =
      WebGeoDS.Dashboard.find("network-from-lines");

    dash?.map?.highlight("network-nodes-py", [Number(id)]);

    dash?.diagram?.setSelected(id);

  }

  // Not assigned to a variable: nothing in this file needs to reach
  // into the instance directly anymore -- selectNode() above looks it
  // up fresh via WebGeoDS.Dashboard.find() instead, and both halves
  // of the cross-link are declared inside the config itself
  // (layers[].onClick, diagram.onNodeClick).
  new WebGeoDS.Dashboard({
    tool: "network-from-lines",
    mount: "#nfl-dashboard",
    map: { center: [12.46, 41.906], zoom: 14 }, // height: Dashboard's own responsive default (see DEFAULT_MAP_HEIGHT, shared/dashboard.js)
    // Just the empty slot beside the map -- filled below by
    // compute.diagram (the force-directed topology view), not by
    // anything declared here. layout.sidePanel doesn't know or care
    // what ends up inside it: it could equally be a second map, a
    // Vega-Lite chart, or nothing at all.
    layout: { sidePanel: { id: "nfl-diagram", flex: "1 1 280px", minWidth: "260px" } },
    upload: { languages: ["python"], kind: "vector", label: "📁 Upload" },
    example: {
      cellId: "network-example-py",
      kind: "geojson",
      status: "✓ example data loaded — try Build Graph, then raise the snap tolerance."
    },
    inspect: {
      cellId: "network-inspect-py",
      layers: [
        { source: "network-input-py", from: (v) => v.features, type: "line", fit: true }
      ],
      stats: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        const rows = [["Lines", s ? s.count.toLocaleString() : "—"]];
        if (s && s.dropped > 0) rows.push(["Non-line features skipped", s.dropped]);
        if (v.crsWarning) rows.push(["CRS", v.crsWarning]);
        return rows;
      }
    },
    compute: {
      cellId: "network-build-py",
      label: "▶ Build graph",
      busyLabel: "⌛ Building...",
      inputs: [
        { kind: "slider", name: "snapTolerance", label: "Snap tolerance (m)",
          range: [0, 20], value: 0, step: 1 }
      ],
      layers: [
        { source: "network-edges-py", from: (v) => v.edges, type: "line",
          paint: (v) => WebGeoDS.matchPaint(v.componentIds, "component", { line: true, lineWidth: 3 }),
          fit: true },
        { source: "network-nodes-py", from: (v) => v.nodes, type: "circle",
          paint: (v) => WebGeoDS.matchPaint(v.componentIds, "component", { radius: 5 }),
          // Map -> diagram half of the cross-link (the diagram -> map
          // half is the diagram config's own onNodeClick below) --
          // declared right next to the layer it belongs to, instead
          // of reaching into the map instance directly after ready().
          onClick: (feature) => selectNode(feature.properties.node) }
      ],
      stats: (v) => {
        const s = v.summary;
        return [
          ["Nodes", s.nodes.toLocaleString()],
          ["Edges", s.edges.toLocaleString()],
          ["Connected components", s.components],
          ["Largest component (nodes)", s.largestComponentNodes],
          ["Dead ends (degree 1)", s.deadEnds],
          ["Intersections (degree ≥ 3)", s.intersections],
          ["Mean degree", s.meanDegree],
          ["Total length", `${s.totalLengthKm} km`],
          ["Snap tolerance", `${s.snapTolerance} m`],
          ["Calculation CRS", s.calculationCrs]
        ];
      },
      legend: (v) => v.componentIds.map((id, i) => ({
        color: WebGeoDS.DEFAULT_PALETTE[i % WebGeoDS.DEFAULT_PALETTE.length],
        label: `Component ${id + 1}`
      })),
      download: {
        // Tags each feature with kind: "node"/"edge" so the two are
        // easy to filter back apart in QGIS or similar after download
        // -- geometry type (Point vs LineString) alone works too, but
        // an explicit property is one click instead of an expression.
        getFeatures: (v) => ({
          type: "FeatureCollection",
          features: [
            ...v.nodes.features.map((f) => ({ ...f, properties: { ...f.properties, kind: "node" } })),
            ...v.edges.features.map((f) => ({ ...f, properties: { ...f.properties, kind: "edge" } }))
          ]
        }),
        filenameSuffix: "-graph.geojson",
        defaultFilename: "network-graph.geojson"
      },
      // The topology diagram: same nodes/edges as the map, laid out by
      // force instead of geography -- answers "how is this connected",
      // which is easy to lose track of on the map once things overlap.
      // A pure function of the compute value, same as layers/stats/
      // legend above -- Dashboard renders it into the layout.sidePanel
      // slot (declared near the top of this config) and owns its
      // create/destroy lifecycle.
      diagram: {
        nodes: (v) => v.nodes,
        links: (v) => v.edges,
        nodeColor: (f) => WebGeoDS.DEFAULT_PALETTE[(f.properties.component ?? 0) % WebGeoDS.DEFAULT_PALETTE.length],
        linkColor: (f) => WebGeoDS.DEFAULT_PALETTE[(f.properties.component ?? 0) % WebGeoDS.DEFAULT_PALETTE.length],
        onNodeClick: (id) => selectNode(id)
      }
    }
  });

});
</script>
